newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slump on U.S. indicators.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slump on U.S. indicators.

text.p: Argentine bonds were much lower late morning Friday after a strong U.S. jobless reports pushed U.S. Treasury yields higher.
A strong U.S. July National Association of Purchasing Managers Index compounded the sharp rise in U.S. Treasury yields. The U.S. 30-year yield rose nine basis points to 6.40 percent.

"It is a very difficult day because we are at critical price levels," said a trader at a foreign bank, pointing to the low spreads and high prices of Argentine bonds that have had some players fearing a sell-off.
Of Argentine bonds, the Par bond was the hardest hit, dropping 6/8 to 75-3/8.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was down $0.63 at 118.25.
"I think many people are being hurt by this downturn," said another trader.
Traders underlined that the difficulty of the market now is its very high levels rather than fundamentals which continue to be supportive.
Still, the second trader said that his medium- and long-term outlook remained bullish.
